_doc: Known Windows test failures, recorded so the ci.yml windows job can gate on everything else. Every test listed here still RUNS on every Windows row, in a separate advisory step that reports it as a warning; it just does not fail the job. A test NOT listed here that fails on Windows fails the job. Remove an entry when its fix lands (the advisory step prints a notice when every listed test for a skill passes). slugs '*' applies to every connector; tests are top-level Go test names. Read by tools/maintainer/windows_known_failures.py.

entries.why: The Windows credential-permission check (internal/cliutil/creds_perms_eval.go, press 4.30.2 and later) compares SDDL text. The built-in local Administrator account (RID 500) renders as the alias LA, never as its S-1-5-21-...-500 SID, so a credentials or config file the CLI itself just wrote is refused as 'token file owner is not the current user'. The GitHub windows-latest account is that account; so is the local Administrator MSP techs use on servers. For them auth set-token saves and then refuses the token, and every MCP or CLI call answers 'stored credentials refused'.
entries.fix: Press: compare SIDs, not SDDL strings (resolve two-letter aliases with ConvertStringSidToSid, or walk the ACL with EqualSid), and add an LA case to TestEvalCredsSecurity. Then reprint or hand-fix creds_perms_eval.go per connector.

entries.why: Hand-written tests that save credentials, so they hit WIN-CREDS-RID500-ALIAS through the generated check.
entries.fix: Fixed by the WIN-CREDS-RID500-ALIAS fix; no test change needed.

entries.why: Press 4.30.1 internal/platform/profile.go refuses any client profile whose Unix mode is not 0600; Windows always reports 0666. Inert today (no tenant identity adapter is registered), and fatal for client profiles once one is.
entries.fix: Reprint on press 4.30.2 or later, which splits the check into perms_windows.go.

entries.why: The test asserts a Unix permission bit (Perm() == 0o600) or relies on a read-only directory refusing writes; Windows reports 0666 and ignores read-only on directories.
entries.fix: Guard the assert with runtime.GOOS != "windows" (or assert the Windows ACL instead).

entries.why: The test isolates the store by setting only HOME. On Windows os.UserHomeDir reads USERPROFILE, so the code reads the runner's real profile (and tests pollute each other through it).
entries.fix: Set USERPROFILE alongside HOME, or use the press testenv.Isolate helper.

entries.why: Eight helper processes write one store at once; one exited 4 (a non-busy write error) on Windows. The same generated test passed in the 12 other connectors that carry it, so this reads as load-dependent, not deterministic.
entries.fix: Have the helper print its error before exiting 4, then re-run; if it reproduces, it is the CLI and MCP server writing one store concurrently on Windows.
